title: REPORT on the Council position on the draft general budget of the European Union for the financial year 2026
part_text: 16. Is seriously concerned that part of EURI's financial needs in 2026 are in fact due to liquidity management costs in 2025; notes that, for the first time, liquidity management costs have increased significantly due to delays in payment requests; stresses that liquidity management costs represent an additional burden in a context of extremely limited resources; regrets that the currently estimated liquidity management costs of EUR 300 million for 2026 would consume around half of the total available funds (including margins and special instruments) in the general budget; In this context, requests that liquidity management costs be separated into a new budget line in order to ensure increased transparency; is firmly convinced that the Commission should find additional resources within existing revenues by proposing cuts in non-essential programmes, rather than introducing new own resources such as the ETS2 system, which will drastically increase the cost of living for Union citizens;
